q: Right ventricular hypertrophy is seen in all EXCEPT:
e: PDA causes LVH (volume load of the left heart).

q: Regarding left-to-right shunts, which is NOT true?
o: ECG in PDA shows right ventricular hypertrophy
e: PDA shows LVH; RVH only with pulmonary hypertension.

q: Which congenital lesion is least likely to cause infective endocarditis?
e: Low pressure gradient across an ASD.

q: An accentuated (loud) pulmonary second sound in a child with a large VSD indicates:
A parasternal heave is NOT expected in:
e: Parasternal heave means RVH; PDA loads the left ventricle.

A 9-year-old has headache and BP 150/95 in the arm; femoral pulses are weak and delayed. The diagnosis is:

q: A preterm infant on day 5 has a systolic murmur below the left clavicle, bounding pulses and is hard to wean from the ventilator. Treatment is:
e: Medical closure of PDA in preterms.
